title: Chapter 2 Revision: Family & mieć
description: Mixed questions covering Chapter 2 grammar (mieć, nominative plural, possessives, genitive singular) and family vocabulary.

questions.explanation: Second person plural (wy = you all) uses macie. 'Wy macie dużo czasu' = You (all) have a lot of time.

questions.prompt: What is the correct nominative plural of 'okno' (window)?
questions.explanation: Neuter nouns ending in -o form their plural with -a: okno → okna.

questions.prompt: To jest ___ mama. (This is my mum.) [mama = feminine]
questions.explanation: 'Mama' is feminine → possessive agrees: 'moja'. 'To jest moja mama' = This is my mum.

questions.prompt: Nie ma ___ w domu. (Dad is not at home.) [tata → ?]
questions.explanation: 'Nie ma' requires the genitive case. 'Tata' (masculine, ends -a) → genitive 'taty'. 'Nie ma taty w domu'.

questions.prompt: How do you say 'I don't have a brother' in Polish?
questions.explanation: 'Nie mam brata' = I don't have a brother. 'Nie mam' = I don't have (1st sg. negation). 'Brata' is genitive after negation.
After 'do' (to), use genitive: siostra (feminine -a) → siostry. 'Jadę do siostry' = I'm going to my sister's.

questions.prompt: What is the virile (masculine personal) plural of 'student'?
questions.explanation: 'Student' → 'studenci' in the virile plural (t → c softening). This is the nominative plural for a group of male or mixed students.

questions.prompt: To jest ___ auto. (This is their car.) [auto = neuter, owners = male]
questions.explanation: 'Ich' = their (possessive for they — both oni and one). 'Ich' is indeclinable — it stays the same regardless of the noun's gender.
